purpose: Concluded findings with their scope limits. Check before proposing a hypothesis. Source of truth; README.md is generated from this file.

findings.question: Does the registered uniform-feasible PIMC configuration beat the development reference?
findings.scope: uniform_feasible_pimc_small_v1 with world_count=4, showing search enabled, rollout policy partner_aware_v1, match_transition utility; 32 complementary complete-match pairs from 0-0 against development_reference_v1.
does_not_establish: The registry states it explicitly: no strength claim is made or implied about PIMC designs in general. ONE CONFIGURATION was measured, not a family.
Every registered configuration ever evaluated used world_count <= 8. See c3-world-count: delta is cleared only at 64, and 4 is slightly NEGATIVE.
It searched every trick-play decision; see c4-opening-lead-specific for where headroom actually is.
Its rollout policy was partner_aware_v1, not the incumbent partner_aware_lead_v2, which is not a supported rollout policy.

findings.question: Can search-local state remove engine revalidation cost without changing search semantics?
findings.scope: Phase 5D-B search semantics only. fast_trick search-local trick-play state, differential-tested against the authoritative engine.
does_not_establish: It was NOT applied to the Phase 5C PIMC rollout path: rollout.py does not use fast_trick, while multi_observer.py and root_info_uct.py do.
The speedups are for 5D-B semantics; the magnitude on other search families is an estimate until measured.

findings.question: What observation-compatible headroom exists at the forehand's first show?
findings.scope: 512 forehand hands x 128 exact conditional completions x 2 arms; alternative arm is a declared lowest-eligible-rank selector; frozen reference continuation; 0-0; equity endpoint, delta 0.001.
does_not_establish: INCONCLUSIVE ONLY BECAUSE OF A PRE-REGISTRATION DEFECT: the declared bound's noise allowance was 10x delta, so its gate could never fire. This is not evidence about the game.
Nothing about card play, which is 95.3% of decisions.
Nothing about a freely chosen alternative card, later showing seats, non-zero scores, or transfer to other policies.

findings.question: How many of the reference's decisions can change the deal outcome at all?
findings.scope: Reference self-play, frozen continuation, decisions across whole deals.

findings.question: Where does the incumbent's hindsight loss sit, and is it concentrated?
findings.scope: 96 deals, 2613 evaluated-partnership decisions, hindsight loss = best legal action minus chosen, own continuation, all four seats the incumbent.
does_not_establish: Hindsight loss is an UPPER BOUND on addressable loss: the best action is identified using the actual hidden hands. See s1b-showing-kill for a measured 65x gap at showing.
Self-play blind spot: a flaw both partnerships share is invisible.
The pre-registered concentration criterion was share-based and could not fire for a small intense class.

findings.question: Does E1's post-hoc intensity gradient replicate on fresh seeds with bars fixed in advance?
findings.scope: 192 fresh-seed deals, 5264 decisions, cluster bootstrap by deal, three hypotheses with bars declared before the run.
does_not_establish: Showing being a high-hindsight-intensity class does NOT make it a target: s1b-showing-kill had already killed the showing intervention, and the 96%-irreducible finding explains the intensity.
NOLO did not replicate and is not a licensed target.
Hindsight metric, so the same upper-bound caveat as e1-loss-map.

findings.question: Does the signed-deal-points surrogate point the same way as match outcomes?
findings.scope: Three contrasts at zero, moderate and extreme effect; deal mode 96 units, match mode 24 units, supply 256, both endpoints on independent banks.
does_not_establish: Directional agreement only. RANK agreement - whether the surrogate orders candidates the same way - is unestablished and is what acceptance decisions need.
No conversion factor between the endpoints is asserted.
The two endpoints were measured on independent banks, so this is a sign comparison, not a paired one.

findings.question: Repeat S1 with the shrinkage estimator declared in advance: is there fundable headroom at the first show?
findings.scope: Fresh seeds, same design as S1: forehand's FIRST show, alternative card chosen by a declared lowest-eligible-rank selector, frozen reference in all other seats, 0-0, equity endpoint, delta 0.001.
does_not_establish: Nothing about card play, 95.3% of decisions and untouched.
Nothing about a FREELY CHOSEN alternative card; the rules permit up to 26 legal showing actions and only one alternative was tested.
Nothing about later showing seats, which decide after observing passes.
Nothing about non-zero scores; equity is convex in the score and this is 0-0 only.
Nothing about transfer: every seat was the reference.
Nothing about whether a learned player is possible.
It does NOT bound a joint showing/play policy: this is a marginal test under reference continuation.

findings.question: How much of the reference's strategy can be tested by single-rule ablation?
findings.scope: The reference's own HeuristicProfile switch surface, established before any performance measurement.

findings.question: Are the reference's public-inference deductions sound?
findings.scope: Hard ownership exclusions, checked against true deals. Also tested a behavioural ducking deduction.
does_not_establish: The behavioural ducking deduction is NOT sound and the reference does not implement it; soundness applies only to the hard exclusions.

findings.question: Does disabling any single ablatable rule of the reference improve it?
findings.scope: 2000 control deals, the 4 ablatable rules plus one compound control, equity endpoint, delta 0.001, exploratory one-sided 95%.
does_not_establish: Nothing about the 12 unvalidated strategic rules that have no ablation switch, which is three quarters of the reference's unvalidated strategy.
Nothing about rule ADDITIONS or modifications, only about disabling existing ones.
Nothing about compound or multi-rule changes beyond the single V5 control.

findings.question: Is there exploitable headroom at the evaluated partnership's first turn in trick 12?
findings.scope: 2000 control deals, every legal action replayed on the ACTUAL hidden deal with the frozen reference continuing. Hidden state used offline only.
does_not_establish: Neither proceeds nor kills: the lower bound does not exceed delta and the upper bound does not fall below it.
This is an ORACLE gain using hidden state, not observation-compatible headroom.
Nothing about other tricks or other decision classes.

findings.question: What observation-compatible headroom exists at the opening card play?
findings.scope: 512 observations x 128 completions x 13 arms, two conditioning models (hard-constraint and policy-dependent), equity endpoint, delta 0.001.
does_not_establish: VOID: G_deploy exceeded G_legal_eb by 2 to 2.5x with disjoint intervals, which is impossible, from two estimator defects - noise treated as independent across arms priced on the same completions, and shrinkage applied across arms rather than across observations.
NO HEADROOM BOUND is claimed by this run. That was its purpose and it failed.
The cross-fitted G_deploy is unaffected by both defects and is the number that carries forward.

findings.question: How many sampled worlds does the opening-lead selector need to clear delta, and what does it cost?
findings.scope: 511 observations, hard-constraint conditioning, W in {1,2,4,8,16,32,64}, cross-fitted G_deploy, equity endpoint, delta 0.001. All three instrument gates passed.
does_not_establish: Only W=64 clears delta; W=1 is actively HARMFUL and W<=4 is negative to negligible.
It is NOT a headroom bound. G_deploy <= G_legal, so 8.5% of foresight is a LOWER bound on legal headroom, not an upper bound on it. The ceiling at the opening lead remains unmeasured.
The curve was still rising at W=64 (32->64 increment +0.000215), so 64 is not the asymptote.
Cost was derived from aggregate batch throughput, not a timed single-decision request latency.
Both arms continue with the frozen reference: this is opening-lead selection, not search play.

findings.question: Does the opening-lead selector's gain generalise to later decisions?
findings.scope: 256 observations, same seat followed through the deal at cards_left 12/9/6/3, W=64, worlds from the validated feasible sampler. All three instrument gates passed, including cross-instrument replication at depth 12.
does_not_establish: Only the opening lead clears delta; depths 9, 6 and 3 are all well below it.
Depth is CONFOUNDED with lead-versus-follow: at later depths the seat was on lead only 13-27% of the time with about five legal cards instead of thirteen. Whether a later LEAD benefits is unmeasured.
No aggregate across depths may be computed: per-decision counterfactuals are not additive (see e6-capture-timing).
Nothing about non-zero scores or transfer beyond the frozen reference.

findings.question: Should the incumbent decline to overtake its partner when an opponent can duck and preserve an honour?
findings.scope: Observational, 192 deals, RAMI trick-play decisions where the partner held the trick and overtaking was legally possible; hindsight loss; stratified by duck availability.
does_not_establish: Observational and confounded: the policy chooses when to overtake, so the groups differ systematically. Enough to refuse the hypothesis, not to endorse the rule.
The catalogued rule it questions, partner.rami.overtake_when_partner_beatable.v1, remains unvalidated (provenance generic_trick_taking_hypothesis).

findings.question: Is winning a trick a liability when no safe lead remains afterwards?
findings.scope: 192 deals; 'no safe exit' operationalised as every remaining card being a certain winner; stratified by cards remaining.
does_not_establish: NOT REFUTED, UNMEASURED: the proxy matched only 1 of the 3 positions that motivated it and collapses into the endgame, where nothing is left to decide.
A forward-looking squeeze measure was never tested; the 1% loss ceiling argues against building one.
The concept as the reviewer stated it - anticipating a future squeeze - remains untested.

findings.question: Should the incumbent hold a certain winner to promote its lower cards in that suit?
findings.scope: 192 deals, RAMI decisions played into a promotion structure; proxy validated against both motivating positions first; then the actual substitution priced by counterfactual.
does_not_establish: The 41.3% figure was SELECTION ON THE OUTCOME: computed among decisions that already carried loss, while the rule fires on the whole population including the 56.3% where the policy was already right.
Three converging signals - a 3x association, the named alternative being hindsight-best, and expert reasoning - all pointed the wrong way. Only pricing the counterfactual caught it.
One band (opening play, n=63) was positive and is recorded as a possible narrow hypothesis, not a finding.

findings.question: Can one expert, blinded, beat the incumbent on hindsight-flagged decisions, and does their reasoning name rules the catalogue lacks?
findings.scope: 24 trick-play positions, 12 hindsight-flagged and 12 matched zero-loss controls, three-way blinded, formal observation only, one reviewer.
does_not_establish: NOT DETECTED on the efficacy question, but the control arm was near-automatic (91% by chance) so it could not confirm reviewer competence; that was recovered post-hoc.
The flagged arm needed 8 of 12, a bar 71% above chance, so it can only detect a large signal.
Positions were selected by hindsight loss, which is 65x inflated at showing and 91.5%-plus hidden-information-dominated at the opening lead. The seed was pointed at irreducible positions.
The four concepts it named absent from the catalogue are hypotheses, not validated rules.

findings.question: May a policy use the engine's revalidation-elision device to meet the latency budget?
findings.scope: Architectural constraint stated in the module docstring and enforced by a test.
does_not_establish: No policy may enter trusted_transitions; tests/agents/test_architecture.py fails if any agent module imports it. It is a generation and research device, not a runtime performance switch.
Research instruments and generators MAY use it, as the committed S1 instrument does.
The sanctioned route for a search policy is a validated search-local state, differential-tested; see phase5dc-search-fast-path.

findings.question: What does a policy do when a strategic rule is disabled, and how much of the incumbent is testable?
findings.scope: The incumbent's 24 catalogued rules; T0-T3's 16 unvalidated strategic ones.

numbers.flag_is_identity_safe: 29 rules flipped in memory, zero agent ids moved

does_not_establish: That the seven Class B rules are testable yet; they share score components under disjoint conditions and need per-rule condition-scoped neutralisation.
That the three Class C showing thresholds are ablatable at all; removing a threshold has no neutral meaning and they are better varied than removed.
That any unblocked rule is harmful. Ablation can only find harmful rules, and T2 found none qualified.

findings.question: How much of the opening lead's perfect-information gain is reachable from the observation alone?
findings.scope: Opening lead, HARD conditioning, incumbent continuing every other seat, all deals at score 0-0.
does_not_establish: A ceiling. The increment series is not decaying and the curve had not converged at W=256; the extrapolated plateau adds 63% of the measured value and is unusable.
Irreducibility. G_foresight minus G_legal is the value of hidden information, not an error floor of any policy.
Anything about the incumbent's distance from G_legal; this measures the far end of that interval.
Anything at non-zero score states, which were never varied.

findings.question: Does the measured opening-lead headroom appear when the selector actually plays?
findings.scope: Deployed W=128 opening-lead selector, incumbent delegate and continuation, duplicate design, score states drawn from the match-visit distribution.
does_not_establish: That the effect is absent. The campaign was underpowered by a knowable factor and could not have detected C2's effect.
That the effect is present.
Score-state dependence: the instrument discarded the per-block scores, so its own prediction P3 could not be evaluated.

findings.question: Can an opening-lead PIMC selector run inside the decision bound?
findings.scope: Cold maximum over 12 fresh deals, single host, 13 legal actions.
does_not_establish: The ten-second production requirement, which includes showing, encoding, transfers and synchronisation under a watchdog.
Anything about other hosts.
Any claim about strength.

findings.question: Does the existing cross-play record say anything about whether the incumbent's advantage transfers?
findings.scope: reports/phase4/baseline_report.json, 11 teams, 66 cells.
does_not_establish: Anything about transfer. The report states cross-play uses a deliberately small shared bank and is descriptive only.
Anything about partner_aware_lead_v2, which post-dates this matrix and is absent from it.

findings.question: How differently do the Phase 4 profiles actually play?
findings.scope: Action divergence from partner_aware_v1 over 435 decisions at score 0-0.
does_not_establish: That the profiles are identical in general. match_aware_v1 is inert at 0-0 specifically, because a match-aware policy has nothing to be aware of at a level score; it may differ where the score is not level.
Anything about relative strength; this is divergence of chosen actions, not quality.

findings.question: Does the incumbent's advantage over its predecessor survive an opponent it was not developed against?
findings.scope: Difference in differences, per-deal frozen-continuation equity, duplicate design, 1024 base deals per opponent, all deals at score 0-0.
does_not_establish: Transfer beyond 8.7% opponent divergence. T5 extended the range to 61.5% and found the margin retains only 29-43% of its home value against three rigid opponents; see t5-margin-collapses-against-rigid-opponents.

Transfer to opponents outside the Phase 4 family. T4's opponent set was drawn from that family, whose maximum divergence from the predecessor (8.7%) is below the improvement's own (10.1%). The Phase 3 controls diverge 45-62% and were NOT tested; an earlier version of this entry wrongly said no such opponent existed.
Anything about human opponents.
Anything at non-zero score states; every deal started at 0-0.
Absence of mild degradation: all three foreign margins sit below the control, three of three in the same direction, one-sided sign test p=0.125.

findings.question: Does the incumbent's improvement survive an opponent seven times more foreign than the Phase 4 ladder allows?
findings.scope: Difference in differences, per-deal frozen-continuation equity, duplicate design, 1024 base deals per opponent, 8 opponents spanning 3.7%-61.5% divergence, all deals at 0-0.
does_not_establish: The mechanism. The rule's two pre-named explanations both fail: not saturation, because the weakest opponent has the highest foreign margin; not foreignness, because the most divergent opponent overlaps the control. The rigidity reading in results section 3 was generated after seeing the data and is untested.

Anything about human opponents. A control that always plays the highest legal card is rigid in a way no person is, and the rigidity reading would if anything predict the opposite for a variable human.
That the improvement is harmful anywhere: all eight margins are positive with intervals excluding zero.
Anything at non-zero score states.

evidence_note: Entries beginning docs/ src/ work/ reports/ tests/ manifests/ are repository paths and are existence-checked by tuppi_research.findings.stale_evidence. Absolute paths are external run artifacts outside the repository and are NOT checked; they may go missing without this index noticing.
